title: Quantum Behaviors Are Not Semialgebraic
authors: Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, Chenghua Liu
abstract: The conditional probabilities achievable by local measurements on a shared quantum state in a Bell scenario form the set of quantum behaviors, whose structure was studied by Tsirelson. In 1993, Tsirelson asked whether this set is semialgebraic, that is, describable by finite Boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. This question has remained open. We answer it in the negative: with four binary measurements per party, the set of finite-dimensional quantum behaviors, its closure, and the commuting-operator set are all nonsemialgebraic. More strongly, none admits a finite real-analytic description even locally near a particular classical behavior. These results rule out exact finite semidefinite representations and show that no finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy characterizes these sets exactly.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that the set of quantum correlations achievable via local measurements in a Bell test is fundamentally nonsemialgebraic. By analyzing a specific family of quantum behaviors parameterized by $\alpha$, the authors show that these sets cannot be described by any finite combination of polynomial equations and inequalities. This result has major implications for understanding the mathematical structure of quantum nonlocality.
main_problem: The paper addresses whether the set of quantum behaviors achievable by local measurements in a Bell scenario is semialgebraic, a long-standing open question in quantum foundations.
main_result: The set of quantum behaviors, its closure, and the commuting-operator set are proven to be nonsemialgebraic for the four-input, binary-output scenario.
method: The proof uses contradiction, constructing a specific quadratic curve $p_\alpha$ whose parameters $\alpha$ must belong to a discrete, infinite set, which contradicts the assumption that the set is semialgebraic.
model_or_system: The model is the set of quantum correlations derived from local measurements on a shared quantum state (Bell scenario). The analysis focuses on the structure of these achievable conditional probabilities.
key_observables: The set of quantum behaviors ($C_q$), its closure ($C_{qa}$), and the commuting-operator set ($C_{qc}$), parameterized by $\alpha$.
important_parameters: The number of local measurements (four binary measurements per party) and the parameter $\alpha \in (1, 2)$, which governs the deviation from classicality.
main_assumptions: The results rule out exact finite semidefinite representations and show that no finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy characterizes these sets exactly.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the intersection of the constructed curve $p_\alpha$ with the quantum behavior sets at points $\alpha_m = 2 - 2/m$, showing accumulation at the classical endpoint $p_2$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the quantum behavior sets, constructing a specific curve $p_\alpha$ passing through points corresponding to discrete $\alpha_m$, and then using the properties of semialgebraic sets to derive a contradiction based on the infinite nature of the required points.
why_interesting: This work establishes fundamental mathematical limitations on the description of quantum correlations, showing that they cannot be captured by simple polynomial inequalities, which has implications for characterizing quantum resources.
